description.en:
A topic-wise e-book on the Indian economy for competitive exams — national income, inflation, banking and the RBI, the Union Budget and GST, agriculture and welfare schemes, and the key features of the economy of Assam.

This is an online reading e-book only. It cannot be downloaded as a PDF.

প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে ভাৰতীয় অৰ্থনীতিৰ বিষয়-ভিত্তিক ই-বুক — জাতীয় আয়, মুদ্ৰাস্ফীতি, বেংকিং আৰু ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক, কেন্দ্ৰীয় বাজেট আৰু GST, কৃষি আৰু কল্যাণমূলক আঁচনি, আৰু অসমৰ অৰ্থনীতিৰ মূল বৈশিষ্ট্য।

content.en:
National income measures the total money value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. The important concepts are GDP (Gross Domestic Product), GNP (Gross National Product) and NNP (Net National Product). GDP is the total production within the country, while GNP adds the net income earned from abroad. NNP at factor cost is called National Income.

In India national income is calculated by the Central Statistical Organisation, now known as the National Statistical Office. Since the 2014–15 base year, GDP is measured at market prices and the new series uses the Gross Value Added (GVA) method.

Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level. In India it is measured by the CPI (Consumer Price Index) for retail inflation and the WPI (Wholesale Price Index) for wholesale prices. The Reserve Bank of India now uses the CPI as the main anchor for its monetary policy with a target of 4% with a tolerance band of 2% on either side. Deflation is the opposite of inflation, and stagflation means high inflation with slow growth and high unemployment.

title.as: বেংকিং, ৰিজাৰ্ভ বেংক, বাজেট আৰু GST

content.en:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949, is the central bank of India. It issues currency, controls credit, manages foreign exchange and acts as the banker to the government. Important RBI instruments include the repo rate (rate at which RBI lends to banks) and the reverse repo rate. CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) control the money that banks must keep with the RBI and in liquid assets.

The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister and contains the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government for the coming financial year (April to March). The two parts of a budget are the Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget. A fiscal deficit occurs when total expenditure exceeds total receipts, and the FRBM Act sets targets to control it.

The Goods and Services Tax (GST), introduced on 1 July 2017, is the biggest tax reform of independent India. It unified many indirect taxes into one and is a destination-based consumption tax with the slogan 'One Nation, One Tax'. GST is levied by the Centre and the states together through the GST Council.

Agriculture is the backbone of the Indian economy and employs the largest share of the workforce. The Green Revolution of the 1960s made India self-sufficient in food grains, especially wheat and rice. The Minimum Support Price (MSP) protects farmers from price falls, and the Public Distribution System (PDS) supplies subsidised food through ration shops. Major schemes include PM-KISAN (income support), MGNREGA (employment guarantee) and Kisan Credit Card loans.

The economy of Assam is primarily agrarian, with tea as the most important plantation crop — Assam produces about half of India's tea. Other crops are rice (the staple food), jute, sugarcane and mustard. Assam is also rich in mineral resources; it was the first state in India where oil was struck, at Digboi in 1889, and natural gas is produced at Duliajan.

Assam has abundant forest resources and a traditional handloom economy based on Muga, Pat and Eri silk. The state government has launched flagship schemes such as the Orunodoi scheme (monthly assistance to poor families), Atmanirbhar Asom, and the Mission Basundhara for land rights. However, the state faces challenges of floods, unemployment and limited industrialisation, which are the focus of successive development plans.
